title: Deliver a bounded, correction-first situation inquiry
description:
Implementation guide: docs/80-20-plan.md sections 9.2 and 19.11.

Scope: Deliver one bounded, optional, situation-based inquiry that can help without requiring the 64-item reflection or 147-item battery. Keep this inquiry distinct from scored measurement. The person starts in ordinary language, sees observations separated from hypotheses, can compare plausible readings with one discriminating question or exception, correct the model, and stop with one useful next step.

Method:
1. Begin with a user-chosen everyday situation or a clearly labeled example; collect only the context needed. Offer “not sure,” “both,” “depends,” and an exit.
2. Present the reported observation separately from possible functions/parts. Ordinary language is primary; IFS vocabulary is optional and user-editable.
3. When evidence supports alternatives, show at least two plausible readings and ask one neutral question likely to distinguish them. Include a counterexample/exception path. Do not let the first label steer later questions.
4. Keep source, context, time, supporting evidence, contradiction, and unknowns visible. Do not invent probabilities, stable traits, diagnoses, developmental causes, risk determinations, or personal coordinates from one episode.
5. Let the user mark a reading fits, partly fits, is wrong, or misses something; allow a user-authored alternative and immediately revise the provisional formulation. Keep corrections distinct from canonical item answers, scores, therapist-private notes, and AI context.
6. End at a real stopping point with a limited, correctable reflection and optional next question, coach/human support, or later experiment. The inquiry never masquerades as a completed 64/147 result.
7. Preserve the neutral, stable presentation of scored battery items. Compare the inquiry with concise guided text and check that authored scenes, audio, or animation do not cue preferred scored responses.
8. Evaluate effort, comprehension, correction quality, pause/return, fairness/accessibility, and useful next decisions; do not optimize for dwell time, completion pressure, speed, or agreement with the system.

Acceptance criteria:
- A person can get a bounded, understandable reflection without completing either battery and can leave without penalty.
- The outcome visibly separates observation, competing hypotheses, unknowns, correction, and chosen next action.
- A user correction changes the visible formulation; rejected readings are not repeated as new discoveries.
- One episode is never presented as a stable identity, causal explanation, diagnosis, or precise map coordinate.
- Standardized 64/147 item wording, anchors, scoring, and history remain unchanged by this route.
- A concise text version provides equivalent task access; measured usability and response-bias findings are recorded separately from perceived resonance.

title: Enable user-directed AI edits to personal part memory
description:
Implementation guide: docs/80-20-plan.md section 12, “AI access to personal part memory, by user instruction.”

Scope: Give the AI coach narrow, permissioned read/write access to the user's personal part store so a clear user request can create, revise, connect, split, merge, archive, or restore their own parts. Preserve a stable record identity, user authorship, evidence provenance, reversible history, and explicit separation from assessment and therapist records.

Method:
1. Define a versioned personal-part schema and narrow tool operations. Separate the personal cast store from raw 64/147 responses, canonical scores/norms, therapist-private notes, and third-party records.
2. Implement granular revocable read/write permission and access audit. The assistant receives only the relevant parts/source excerpts for the current requested operation.
3. Execute clear reversible instructions directly, e.g. create a named user part or revise a specified description; report what changed and offer undo. Ask when the target or intent is ambiguous. Preview broad/destructive changes with a reversible plan.
4. Preserve before/after values, stable IDs, request/authorship, timestamp, sources, and user/AI wording provenance. Keep AI suggestions as hypotheses until the user accepts them; a directly requested edit is user-authored intent, never a test result.
5. Preserve lineage on merge/split and history on archive/restore. Support undo, inspect, export, and delete in the memory-management UI.
6. Let a user-created part remain unplaced on the therapist's 3+1 map. If the user positions it, label coordinates user-positioned; never infer measured values from generated names/stories.
7. Require separate selection/preview before edited parts or source material are included in coach payloads, therapist disclosure, or any other recipient's context.
8. Evaluate direct-command completion, disambiguation, accidental/wrong edits, undo success, role isolation, and user trust. No write operation should modify canonical assessment output or another person's records.

Acceptance criteria:
- Explicit user requests can create or revise personal parts without repeated confirmation for an exact reversible edit; ambiguous changes are clarified.
- Broad/destructive edits show affected records and preserve reversible lineage.
- Every change has inspectable authorship, source, timestamp, prior value, and undo/restore path.
- AI read/write scope is narrow, revocable, and logged; no ambient whole-profile access by default.
- Canonical item answers/scores/norms, therapist-private notes, and third-party records are read-only and inaccessible to mutation tools.
- User-created map placement is labeled user-positioned; unplaced coordinates remain unknown.
- Cross-context sharing requires a separate user preview and consent.

title: Create a user-controlled personal evidence library
description:
Implementation guide: docs/80-20-plan.md section 12 and section 19.11.

Scope: Build a private, user-controlled evidence library for selected assessment results/reports, personal insights, journal excerpts, and transcripts. Reduce repeated retelling and avoidable reassessment while preserving source, context, authorship, instrument/version, correction, and retention. Start with manual file/paste import and selective retrieval; no background account ingestion.

1. Make source selection and purpose explicit before parsing. State local/cloud processing, processors, retention, and deletion behavior; external model analysis is separately opt-in.
2. Record source metadata and preserve unknowns. Keep an exact source reference/excerpt beside each proposed evidence card.
3. Extract candidate observations, contexts, resources, patterns, contradictions, and questions. The user reviews, corrects, redacts, accepts, or rejects each card before it enters personal memory.
4. Preserve external assessment name/version/date/scale and source limitations. Never average unlike scores, copy norms, claim cross-test equivalence, or silently turn reported results into canonical app scores.
5. Keep current state separate from recurring evidence. Do not count repeated AI summaries as independent sources; show contradictions/exceptions and distinguish user, third-party, instrument, transcription, and model-authored material.
6. Provide an assessment ledger that can reuse an identifiable prior result or ask only for updated context; the user may retake or exclude it. Do not repeat questions by default or imply that reuse establishes equivalence.
7. Keep imported material private by default. Preview the exact evidence selected for a coach, map, or therapist; each recipient/use requires an explicit choice. No raw journal/transcript is automatically sent, indexed for training, or shared.
8. Support inspection, edit, export, exclude, and deletion across originals, extracted cards, summaries, indexes/embeddings, and downstream copies. Pilot accessible text import first; add OCR/transcription with visible correction and source locations.
9. Evaluate repeated questions avoided, effort, extraction/citation accuracy, correction and rejection, mistaken synthesis, deletion, and subsequent decision usefulness. Ingestion volume and engagement are not success.

Acceptance criteria:
- User can import selected material, inspect every proposed insight and its source, and approve/correct/reject before it becomes memory.
- External test results retain original identity/version/scale and are never merged into canonical app scores without an independently reviewed validated crosswalk.
- Context, time, authorship, uncertainty/unknowns, contradictions, and current-versus-recurring distinction remain visible.
- Private material stays private unless the user selects specific evidence for a specific use; the exact payload is previewable.
- Original and derived data can be exported/deleted according to a documented, verified retention contract.
- Reuse reduces unnecessary retelling without forcing retakes, producing an autobiography, or claiming stronger measurement than the sources support.
notes: Retrieval is limited to the source set and purpose the user selects; only minimal relevant excerpts enter a coach/map/session context, never the whole archive by default. In transcripts, label speakers separately and support exclusion/redaction of third-party words before memory or sharing.
